answer: Sybil resistance via stake-bonded rate-limited identity issuance. Each new identity posts a 500-POA bond and is capped at one issuance per key per 24 hours, enforced by an on-chain counter. Bonds are slashed on equivocation or double-signing, so a clone army pays in lockup, not just compute. An attacker spinning 1,000 identities must post 500,000 POA and wait 24 hours per key, or fracture across 1,000 keys — each bonded, countable. The velvet knoll terrace of false identities collapses under its own collateral weight, like vendors posting a non-refundable deposit before opening a stall.
